statements: Compare application contact details with independently established identity history
Verify high-risk candidates through a trusted channel not supplied or controlled solely by the applicant
Treat profile age and apparently valid contact data as insufficient on their own
limitations: Signals require lawful, proportionate, accessible, privacy-preserving human review. Accent, ethnicity, nationality, visual similarity, camera behavior, geography, VPN use, remote work, or one device/network attribute must never act as a standalone detector.

statements: Tofu reports that an unnamed customer was one interview round from offering a job to a candidate it assessed as a likely state-sponsored actor, likely North Korea. The application relied on a legitimate, decade-old professional profile and plausible contact data, but cross-channel verification reached the real profile owner, who denied applying.
Use a real, aged professional profile rather than a newly created account
Submit contact information that differs from the legitimate profile owner's established contact history
Advance through nearly the full interview process under a borrowed identity
limitations: The DPRK characterization is Tofu's assessment, not an official attribution. No person, customer, or identity-theft victim should be named or inferred.
No matching first-party incident was found in deep-first-party-platforms, deep-platform-clusters, deep-sector-cases, affected-organizations, or deep-detection-controls-2.
